channel.title: Frontier Wire
channel.description: AI news: frontier labs, research, policy and commentary.

item.title: OpenAI announces new tools and guidance to combat online child sexual abuse
item.description: OpenAI said it will provide new tools, practical guidance and partnerships to help prevent, detect and respond to online child sexual exploitation and abuse. Improved safeguards protect vulnerable users and set standards for AI platforms handling harmful content.

item.title: Nvidia unveils Rubin HPC GPU with over 50,000 CUDA cores for scientific simulations
item.description: At SC26 Nvidia announced the Rubin HPC GPU, part of the Vera Rubin platform, featuring more than 50,000 CUDA cores, sparse data acceleration and seventh‑generation NVLink to speed up agent‑driven simulations for science, engineering and analytics. Faster GPU‑accelerated simulations let AI agents iterate quicker, shortening the path from hypothesis to discovery for researchers and industry designers.

item.title: Corma raises $125 million Series A to scale AI agents for cyber defense
item.description: Corma, a Tel‑Aviv and San Francisco startup that builds custom‑trained AI agents for defensive cybersecurity, closed a $125 million Series A led by NEA, bringing total funding to $185 million and valuing it at $1 billion. The funding underscores rising investor confidence in AI‑driven defensive security tools as enterprises confront increasingly sophisticated cyber threats.

item.title: Jensen Huang allies form "war room" to lobby for his return as Nvidia CEO
item.description: A group of Silicon Valley executives is assembling a "war room" to lobby Nvidia's board to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO, days after he resigned over reports of affairs with a subordinate and a suspected Chinese spy. The public letter demanding his return has gathered over 150,000 signatures, with support from Elon Musk and Tim Sweeney. Nvidia's leadership stability is a key factor for the AI industry, as the company's chips underpin much of the sector's infrastructure.

item.title: Baidu posts sixth straight quarterly sales drop as ad slump offsets AI cloud growth
item.description: Baidu reported Q3 revenue down 1% year-over-year to approximately $4.6 billion, marking its sixth consecutive quarterly sales decline. Net income came in at approximately $210 million (1.4 billion yuan), while AI businesses now make up over 50% of its revenue. Baidu's continued reliance on AI growth to offset legacy search declines illustrates the pressures traditional internet companies face amid broader economic headwinds and increased competition in the AI sector.

item.title: China pushes toward nationwide AI education in schools by 2030
item.description: China is pursuing a national target for universal AI literacy in schools by 2030, supported by over $31 million in government procurement for AI classroom equipment and teaching platforms. Schools are introducing AI-focused curricula to teach programming, robotics, and AI application. This policy highlights a major state-backed effort to integrate artificial intelligence into basic education and build an AI-native generation.

item.title: Startups unveil plans for floating offshore data centers
item.description: Startups are announcing plans to develop floating offshore data centers to bypass land and power constraints. Experts have warned of challenges including saltwater corrosion. This trend highlights how infrastructure providers are exploring alternative environments to address terrestrial power and land limitations.

item.title: LVMH media division adopts ChatGPT Enterprise alongside internal AI platform
item.description: LVMH’s media division is deploying OpenAI's ChatGPT Enterprise to its teams. The luxury group already operates its own internal multi-model platform, MaIA, which had about 50,000 users as of mid-2026. The deal shows OpenAI securing a direct deployment within a high-profile corporate division even as the parent organization diversifies its AI infrastructure across multiple model providers.

item.title: Oister Global launches ₹600 Cr growth-stage deeptech fund
item.description: Private markets asset manager Oister Global launched a growth-stage deeptech fund with a target corpus of ₹400 Cr and a ₹200 Cr greenshoe option. The fund aims to back 8 to 10 revenue-generating Indian startups across sectors including space, defence, and semiconductors. The fund targets a funding gap for growth-stage deeptech startups in India that have moved past early-stage development but struggle to find committed institutional investors.

item.title: Anthropic IPO tests its public benefit commitment
item.description: Anthropic plans an initial public offering this month while maintaining its status as a public benefit corporation. Experts highlight that its governance structure leaves wide leeway in measuring its commitment to society. The company's upcoming public offering highlights the tension between maximizing financial returns and maintaining public benefit commitments for multi-trillion-dollar artificial intelligence firms.

item.title: OpenAI partners with independent evaluators for safety pilots
item.description: OpenAI signed agreements with four independent evaluators—Apollo Research, METR, Transluce, and Goodfire—to conduct pilot assessments on model behavior and safeguards. The organizations will receive deep access to OpenAI's internal systems as part of the safety work. The move brings independent researchers inside frontier AI labs to monitor safety and alignment risks as models grow more capable.

item.title: Indonesian police raided Nvidia partner Megaspeed local unit in early 2026
item.description: Indonesian police raided the office of Nvidia partner Megaspeed's local subsidiary in early 2026 at the request of U.S. authorities. Officers found unopened server racks but no graphics processing units during the FBI-requested inquiry. This event highlights international scrutiny over the distribution pathways of advanced artificial intelligence hardware subject to U.S. export restrictions.

item.title: Zus Health raises $33M Series B to build healthcare AI data platform
item.description: Zus Health raised $33 million in Series B funding led by Drive Capital to build data infrastructure for AI-powered clinical workflows. The financing brings the company's total funding to more than $100 million. This funding highlights how investors are backing foundational data infrastructure companies aiming to supply clean, connected records for healthcare AI applications and agents.

item.title: Sumary raises $25M seed round to expand AI accounting software in Europe
item.description: Copenhagen-based AI accounting software startup Sumary has raised $25M in a seed round led by Singular, bringing its total funding to $29.2M. The company plans to use the capital to expand across Europe and establish a commercial hub in London. The funding highlights growing investor interest in applying AI automation to traditional professional services like accounting to address labor shortages and repetitive workflows.

item.title: SEBI to issue guidelines for AI use and human oversight in capital markets
item.description: SEBI will soon issue guidelines requiring market firms to disclose AI usage and maintain human oversight over critical decisions, according to SEBI Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey. The upcoming framework aims to protect investors and maintain market integrity without compromising safety. It shows how financial regulators are moving to enforce accountability and transparency on AI tools used in trading and advisory services.

item.title: OpenAI launches computer-use agents and plugins for healthcare teams
item.description: OpenAI announced new computer-use agents that can operate across healthcare software, along with improved clinical answer capabilities and new healthcare plugins. The tools are intended to help healthcare teams get real work done. It marks a step toward AI systems that can directly interact with clinical applications, potentially streamlining workflows.

item.title: Trump administration plans to name AI "national champions"
item.description: The Trump administration plans to designate more than two dozen artificial intelligence companies, including Nvidia, Amazon, Microsoft, OpenAI, and Anthropic, as "national champions." The program is designed to help U.S. firms expand overseas and compete with Chinese rivals. This policy establishes formal government backing for select U.S. technology firms to help them compete internationally.

item.title: Apple launches Health AI Usage Study app powered by OpenEvidence
item.description: Apple launched the Health AI Usage Study app, developed with OpenEvidence, to examine how users interact with clinically grounded health answers. The study aims to enroll up to 200,000 U.S. participants for over 12 months. The study signals Apple's approach to incorporating clinically sourced AI responses and HealthKit data into user experiences while maintaining privacy controls.

item.title: Alibaba releases Qwen4-Max flagship model
item.description: Alibaba released Qwen4-Max, a new flagship 2.4T-parameter Mixture of Experts model featuring a 1-million-token context window. The company states it beats Qwen3.8-Max using up to ~50% fewer tokens. The release introduces a new high-capacity model with a large context window and improved token efficiency compared to the previous version.

item.title: Nvidia interim CEO Colette Kress expected to rein in deals
item.description: Interim CEO Colette Kress is expected to rein in deals and slow AI investing after a period where Nvidia aggressively financed computing deals and startup investments. Neoclouds and related segments account for nearly half of Nvidia's revenue. A shift in Nvidia's financing strategy could alter growth and funding for neoclouds that rely on the company as a financial safety net.

item.title: Mount Thor raises $45 million to build cloud infrastructure on Apple silicon
item.description: Mount Thor raised $45 million across seed and Series A rounds to build cloud infrastructure for agentic AI on Apple silicon. The startup provides Mac data-center compute instances for macOS workloads. This funding supports the expansion of cloud infrastructure dedicated to running macOS and Apple silicon workloads at data-center scale for AI agents.

item.title: Samsung SDS seeks Anthropic and OpenAI as tenants for AI data centre services
item.description: Samsung’s IT arm, Samsung SDS, is in early talks to sign Anthropic and OpenAI as tenants for its AI data centre business, aiming to offer end‑to‑end building, operation and power services. Securing leading AI model providers as tenants could make Samsung a central hub for AI infrastructure, influencing how companies access compute resources.

item.title: Indian chip startup Bharat Semi lands $24M seed round for AI sensors
item.description: Indian semiconductor startup Bharat Semi has raised $24 million in seed funding to develop AI-enabled image sensors and target commercial production in 2027. The pre-revenue company has secured design wins with General Atomics and Kaynes Semicon. The funding highlights how Indian hardware startups are attracting venture investment to build specialized artificial intelligence chips for global markets amid broader government efforts to establish a domestic semiconductor industry.

item.title: Anthropic targets up to $90.4B in IPO and private placement
item.description: Anthropic's IPO is approximately 7x oversubscribed as the company and its backers seek to raise up to $90.4 billion via an IPO and private placement. The AI firm is targeting a fully diluted valuation of approximately $1.4 trillion. This event represents the largest IPO of all time, drawing immense institutional demand and testing market appetite for AI frontier model makers.

item.title: Huawei's Horinger AI data center has ~7% of Colossus 2 compute
item.description: Epoch AI analysis shows Huawei's Horinger data center holds about 7% of the computing power of xAI's Colossus 2 campus. Horinger is estimated to have roughly 81,000 H100-equivalent units of compute compared to Colossus 2's 1,112,000 units. It highlights the scale gap between flagship AI infrastructure in China and the US.

item.title: A step toward defining the Standard Model on a lattice
item.description: OpenAI explored a candidate nonperturbative lattice definition of the Standard Model. GPT-6 Astra helped turn the idea into a detailed proof. This research explores the use of AI to help develop detailed mathematical proofs in physics.

item.title: Nvidia considers leadership options after Jensen Huang's departure
item.description: Nvidia's board approached Arm Holdings CEO Rene Haas as a potential successor following Jensen Huang's resignation. CFO Colette Kress is currently serving as interim CEO. The leadership transition at Nvidia marks a major shift for the chipmaker at the center of the artificial intelligence boom.

item.title: Megaspeed says Alice Huang left in 2025 amid US probe into Nvidia chip sales
item.description: Singapore-based Megaspeed announced that former executive Alice Huang departed in August 2025 and holds no current role, defending its operations as lawful. The company purchased billions of dollars in Nvidia chips between 2024 and 2026, prompting a U.S. Commerce Department inquiry into potential export control violations. The investigation highlights heightened scrutiny over global AI chip supply chains and follows the abrupt resignation of Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang.

item.title: Jensen Huang discusses Nvidia CEO comeback as allies lobby for return
item.description: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has reportedly discussed returning to lead the chipmaker with confidants, as allies form a lobbying effort for his reinstatement. Huang resigned following an investigation into personal relationships that involved an executive at Megaspeed. The potential return of a long-standing CEO after a major governance and security scandal impacts leadership stability at the world's most valuable public chipmaker.

item.title: Congress moves to tighten export rules on AI chips after Nvidia spy scandal
item.description: Following revelations regarding former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with a suspected Chinese spy, US lawmakers are pushing for stricter export controls on advanced AI chips. Both Democrats and Republicans are reviewing legislative measures and demanding public testimony from industry and government leaders. The political fallout from the Nvidia scandal could accelerate bipartisan efforts to reshape US technology export policies and restrict foreign access to advanced AI hardware.
